error_examples.text: Ordered 304 stainless round bar 1" and the tag on the bundle says 304 but a spot check with the magnet and a spark test says this is mild steel. Can't use plain carbon anywhere near the filler line. Credit it out please, and I'd recommend somebody check that bin.
error_examples.truth: Wrong part in the right bag
error_examples.evidence: the tag on the bundle says 304 but a spot check with the magnet and a spark test says this is mild steel

error_examples.text: Put maybe 20 of your 1/2-13 grade 8 cap screws into engine mount brackets and had two snap right at the head before I got anywhere near spec torque, calibrated wrench. That's not a grade 8 in my book. I want the lot credited, I'm not risking the rest of them on a customer boat.
error_examples.evidence: snapped at the head before I got anywhere near spec torque

error_examples.text: Grabbed a fresh tube of the anaerobic pipe sealant for a chiller repair and the nozzle wouldn't dispense, plunger wouldn't move at all. Cut the tube open and the whole thing is set up solid inside. Need an RMA, I've got five more tubes from the same buy that I don't trust.
error_examples.truth: Assembly or mechanism failure on first use
error_examples.evidence: the whole thing is set up solid inside

error_examples.text: Shop says the 1/4-20 threaded rod came in with ragged ends and torn thread crests - they're having to file each piece before a nut will start, and one of the students caught a hand on it. Can somebody phone me, I need to decide whether to keep the rest of the lot.
error_examples.evidence: ragged ends and torn thread crests

error_examples.text: Snapped the 5/32 hex bit off inside a cap screw at about half the rated torque on a jig build - clean break right at the shank. That's maybe the fifth fastener it had seen. These are supposed to be S2 and they're behaving like pot metal, I want the set credited.
error_examples.evidence: snapped the 5/32 hex bit off... at about half the rated torque

error_examples.text: We ordered the timing belt for our turntable drive and right out of the package it's got a hard set in it — won't lay flat, and when we ran it the whole drive pulsed and the tensioner chattered. Never got past ten minutes of running. Honestly not sure if I want another one or my money back, tell me what makes sense.
error_examples.truth: Assembly or mechanism failure on first use
error_examples.evidence: right out of the package it's got a hard set in it — won't lay flat

error_examples.text: Torquing down the 3/8-16 silicon bronze bolts on a strut mount and one popped the head clean off well under spec. Two others the socket rounded out with a brand new allen key. Just noting it, we swapped to what we had on the shelf.
error_examples.evidence: popped the head clean off well under spec

error_examples.text: Hi, hoping you can help. The 1/4 NPT pressure gauge we got reads about 6 psi with nothing connected to it, and it doesn't settle back. Not sure if it took a knock somewhere along the line. Happy to send it back, we'd just like a replacement when you can - no rush on it.
error_examples.predicted: Assembly or mechanism failure on first use
error_examples.evidence: reads about 6 psi with nothing connected to it, and it doesn't settle back

error_examples.text: can someone give me a call. the 1/8 aluminum sheet we got for mounting plates has a big dent and a wavy edge on one corner, looks like something set on top of it. not sure if you want photos first or what the process is here
error_examples.evidence: has a big dent and a wavy edge on one corner, looks like something set on top of it

error_examples.text: Please give me a call on this. We got a box of 3/8-16 threaded rod and the ends are burred and out of round badly enough that a nut won't start without chasing every one of them. That's 40 pieces I'd have to touch by hand and these are going into a flight hardware fixture so I'd rather not be filing on them.
error_examples.evidence: the ends are burred and out of round badly enough that a nut won't start without chasing every one of them
